title: Universal Mind pilot
design: Single-arm feasibility pilot with repeated before-and-after observations
briefing: This pilot explores how a ten-minute electronic music television experience relates to hypothesised short term stress reduction and increased connection. It brings together EMDR, brain entrainment and sub-audible mantra. Findings will help inform future research with young female veterans. Thank you for your valued service today.
requirements: You’ll need a laptop with a working camera, internet, a Bluetooth speaker and three sessions over one week. You can stop at any time.
eligibility: Women aged 18 and over, recruited through personal networks. This first pilot does not require veteran status.

experience.implementation: Existing M8 experience and existing brain entrainment profile; no new sound generator.

analysis.hrv_psd: Exploratory one-minute beat-interval power around 0.1 Hz (0.085–0.115 Hz), with the spectrum and quality retained. Not a HeartMath score or direct baroreflex sensitivity measurement.
analysis.change: 100 * (after - before) / before; unavailable when baseline is zero or either value is missing

compensation_rule: 100 AUD after all three sessions are completed; otherwise zero.
delivery: On demand, three sessions over one week. Suggested times only; livestream presentation is simulated.

pre_music_reflection.placement: After baseline vitals and all baseline self-report questions, before music playback.
pre_music_reflection.delivery: Fixed four-message script, participant-paced, with animated text and a reduced-motion alternative. No typed response is requested.
pre_music_reflection.interpretation: Part of the combined study intervention. Before-and-after observations include the introduction; they do not isolate the effect of music or the reflection. Read/skip choice and script version are recorded per session.

messages.text: Welcome to the session. Before the music drops, let’s clear some mental space.
We're leaning into Empire of the Sun’s lyric:
messages.quote: I can't do well when I think you're gonna leave me but I know I try. Are you gonna leave me now? Can’t you be believing now?

messages.text: We’re gently shining a light on the fear of being abandoned in a relationship—something many of us have experienced. Some might say it’s a part of being human, a part of the human condition.

If it feels comfortable, think of the first person that comes to mind, where you’d like to soften a sense of loss. You don’t need to name them or share anything. Don’t force it. Just allow. And remember, this too shall pass. Let’s begin.
